paragraph: Allendale is a single-family town, and the numbers there are unambiguous: 22 sales over six months at a median of $1,085,750, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.046, roughly 68% of homes closing above asking, and a median of 12 days on market. That is a real seller's market with multiple offer situations behind a lot of those closings. Sale prices ran from $550,000 to $2.9 million, so the median is the better guide than the average. Condos and townhouses are a thin slice at 7 sales with a median of $900,000, and they moved on the same 12 day clock with an even higher ratio at 1.06. Seven sales is a small sample, so treat that median as a rough marker rather than a benchmark. Most months here carried fewer than five closings, so month-to-month medians are noise. What is readable is volume: June and July together account for more than half the single-family activity, which is exactly where Bergen County's seasonal peak lands. If the usual pattern holds, expect closings to thin out through fall.
